purpose: Doxepin is used to treat depression and anxiety. At a lower dose, it is also used to help people who have trouble staying asleep. A cream form is used on the skin to relieve itching from certain skin conditions.
how_it_works: Doxepin works by balancing certain natural chemicals in your brain, like serotonin and norepinephrine, which help regulate your mood and emotions. It also blocks certain receptors in the brain that help promote sleep when used at a low dose. Think of it as helping your brain's messaging system work more smoothly so you feel better and can rest.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or feeling sleepy is very common, especially at first. You may also notice dry mouth, constipation, blurry vision, dizziness when standing up, weight gain, or difficulty urinating. These effects often improve after the first few weeks.
warnings: Do not stop taking doxepin suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms. It can cause serious heart rhythm problems at higher doses. It may increase thoughts of suicide in children, teens, and young adults, especially early in treatment — contact your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, heart problems, or an enlarged prostate. Do not take it if you have taken an MAO inhibitor in the past 14 days.
typical_dosing: For depression or anxiety, the usual starting dose is 25 to 75 mg per day, often taken at bedtime or split into smaller doses. Doctors may slowly increase this up to 300 mg per day if needed. For sleep problems, a much lower dose of 3 to 6 mg is taken about 30 minutes before bed. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
